decisions.executionNote: Initialize smooth elbow-up approaches. Tentatively assign pens to white, cameras to blue, cars to red; approach left camera and right gold car without crossing.
Align open grippers over left camera and gold vehicle; continue tilting down while approaching, with clearance before grasp.
Fine approach to camera and gold car from wrist images, then close both grippers. Retention remains to be checked on lifting.
Lift both closed grasps before transporting camera toward blue basket and gold vehicle toward red; inspect retention after clearance.
Both objects visibly retained. Replan after continuity rejection using smaller combined forward/lowering increments over assigned baskets.
Objects visibly over basket interiors. Release at current reachable poses, allow settling, then withdraw back/up rather than extending farther.
First camera and gold car now visibly released in blue/red baskets. Withdraw and align above remaining camera and wooden vehicle; keep hands separated.
Descend toward remaining camera and wooden car with small forward corrections from wrist views, keeping both grippers open for visual alignment.
Finish short descent and close around the remaining camera and wooden car. Will verify retention by lifting, not commanded gripper state.
Lift closed grasps clear of the table, then begin moving camera to blue and wooden car to red. Watch for retained objects and continuity limits.
Both second objects visibly retained. Carry them forward over blue and red baskets with smaller left-arm increments near its reach margin.
Move retained objects slightly farther inside basket rims and lower gently. Reduce downward tilt slightly to preserve reach margin before release.
Open both grippers over basket interiors, allow the camera and wooden vehicle to settle, and withdraw with clearance. Remaining pens will go into white.
Two cameras and two vehicles appear inside their separate baskets. Approach black pen with left gripper rotated across its shaft; retract right arm toward home.
Lower open left gripper around black pen shaft with a small forward adjustment. Continue smooth elbow-up return of the right arm.
Fine lateral centering on black pen, close left gripper and start a small retention-test lift. Finish right-arm return near origin.
Lift the closed pen grasp for visual retention checking, then start toward the white basket. Hold the right arm at home.
Black pen remained on the table: reopen and retry with a lower, laterally corrected approach rather than assuming retention.
Pen is now nearly centered between open jaws; relieve table contact slightly, close at the shaft, then make a short test lift.
Black pen appears between closed fingers after the test lift. Lift clear and move toward white basket while checking that it stays in the gripper.
Black pen is visibly retained. Carry it forward into the white basket interior, maintaining orientation and clearance.
Release black pen over white basket, pause to settle, then retreat toward the last yellow-accent pen and rotate jaws across its shaft.
Black pen is visibly settled in white. Approach the last pen's barrel with open jaws oriented perpendicular to its shaft, stopping above final grasp depth.
Use wrist view to correct the last pen's lateral offset and descend only two centimeters to grasp height, keeping jaws open for alignment verification.
Final millimeter-scale centering of the yellow-accent pen, close fully and lift three centimeters to verify retention.
Yellow-accent pen appears retained between the fingers. Lift above basket rim height and begin carrying it toward the white basket with the other pen.
The last pen is visibly retained. Carry it over the white basket, preserving grasp orientation and a small clearance above its rim.
Release the final pen inside white, pause for settling, then clear the rim before returning the left arm to origin.
Both pens are visibly settled in white; cameras and vehicles remain separated in blue/red. Begin smooth left-arm return, gradually restoring home orientation while retracting.
Continue the left-arm return along a smooth elbow-up path with open grippers; leave the sorted objects undisturbed.
Finish returning the left end effector to its initial pose in small continuous increments, then pause with both grippers open for settling.
